queries.search_text: site:digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu AI Act timeline obligations high-risk systems August 2026 official
queries.source_title: Guidelines for providers and deployers of AI high-risk systems
queries.proposition: The Commission says certain AI uses in biometrics, critical infrastructure, education and employment face high-risk rules from 2 December 2027, while AI embedded in products such as robotics and industrial machinery follows on 2 August 2028; its current classification guidance is draft, non-binding and intended to guide enforcement.
queries.status: SUPPORTED FOR RULE TIMING AND CLASSIFICATION FRICTION; BUYER DEMAND UNPROVEN
queries.contradiction: The transition was extended and the cited guidance is expressly non-binding, so urgency may be weaker than vendors claim and interpretations may change before final adoption.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Offer a fixed-fee classification-and-evidence sprint to 15 EU vendors or deployers across the named sectors and require three paid deposits tied to a live procurement or release gate.

queries.search_text: site:digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations timeline manufacturers products digital elements official 2026
queries.proposition: From 11 September 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents through the CRA Single Reporting Platform, with an early warning within 24 hours, a fuller notification within 72 hours and later final reports.
queries.status: SUPPORTED FOR MANUFACTURER REPORTING WORKFLOW; BUDGET AND VERTICAL INCIDENCE UNPROVEN
queries.contradiction: A single EU reporting platform may make filing itself inexpensive; value must come from detection, evidence assembly, decision ownership and deadline control rather than form submission.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Run tabletop incidents with ten small EU manufacturers in the target verticals and seek two paid retainers that begin before the first real incident.

concepts.title: HR AI Deal-Gate Dossier
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A fixed-scope evidence service for European recruiting-software vendors turns each live enterprise review into a signed AI-role, high-risk-boundary and control dossier reusable in later deals.
concepts.customer: EU recruiting and workforce-software vendors selling AI-assisted screening or ranking
concepts.loss_event: An enterprise sale stalls, is discounted or is abandoned because neither side can resolve system classification, provider-versus-deployer duties or required controls.
concepts.payer: Vendor chief product officer or compliance lead
concepts.beneficiary: Sales team, buyer risk team and affected job applicants
concepts.authority_holder: Vendor legal or compliance officer who signs the classification position; the buyer retains acceptance authority
concepts.distributor: Employment-law boutiques, HRIS implementers and buyer-side AI governance advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: The software vendor bears lost-sale and compliance exposure; the employer bears deployment risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: Vendor enterprise-sales director for the blocked account
concepts.first_paid_event: A named buyer opens an AI, privacy or model-risk review before contract signature.
concepts.acquisition_route: Referral fee or white-label delivery through employment-law boutiques already pulled into those reviews
concepts.compounding_asset: An anonymized corpus linking feature patterns, contractual roles, buyer objections and accepted evidence packs
hypotheses: Live deal delay is costly enough to fund a fixed-fee sprint.
A reusable evidence pack is accepted by more than one buyer.
Vendors will share redacted review outcomes for corpus improvement.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: final AI Act duties and dates; SOFT INDUSTRY NORM: buyer questionnaires; ASSUMED CONVENTION: dossier portability; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: deal-delay cost must exceed fee.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not portray draft Commission classification guidance as binding law or guarantee that a dossier establishes compliance.

concepts.title: Education AI Tender Evidence Room
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A tender-linked workspace helps assessment and admissions technology suppliers map each AI use to education-risk boundaries, human oversight and source evidence before a school buyer evaluates the bid.
concepts.customer: Small European edtech vendors supplying AI-assisted admissions, assessment or exam-integrity tools
concepts.loss_event: A tender is rejected or delayed because product claims, intended use and human-oversight evidence cannot survive procurement review.
concepts.payer: Vendor bid director or quality lead
concepts.beneficiary: Vendor commercial team, purchasing institution and students subject to decisions
concepts.authority_holder: Vendor quality officer approves the evidence; the education buyer's procurement authority decides admissibility.
concepts.distributor: Public-tender consultants and education-sector systems integrators
concepts.risk_bearer: The vendor bears bid cost and warranty exposure; the institution bears deployment and rights risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: Vendor bid manager for the named tender
concepts.first_paid_event: Tender notice or buyer questionnaire requests AI classification, oversight or governance evidence.
concepts.acquisition_route: Monitor EU education tenders and partner with bid consultancies on a per-submission package
concepts.compounding_asset: A versioned library of tender clauses, use-case boundaries, evidence mappings and buyer acceptance outcomes
hypotheses: Education buyers will request evidence before the 2027 application date.
Bid teams control discretionary compliance-preparation spend.
Accepted mappings can be safely generalized across institutions.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: applicable final AI Act requirements; REPUTATIONAL EXPECTATION: fairness and explainability claims; ASSUMED CONVENTION: early tender gating; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: tender value must justify bespoke work.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not imply every education AI tool is high-risk; intended purpose and actual decision role require case-specific review.

concepts.title: Grid AI Deployer Control Ledger
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A lightweight control ledger lets smaller electricity-network and flexibility operators attach input-data checks, human overrides and incident evidence to each production AI decision workflow.
concepts.customer: Regional distribution-network operators and renewable-flexibility aggregators deploying AI in operational workflows
concepts.loss_event: A production pilot is blocked, rolled back or left unauditable because operational ownership, input-data fitness and override evidence are fragmented.
concepts.payer: OT risk director, innovation director or chief information security officer
concepts.beneficiary: Grid operator, control-room staff, connected generators and energy users
concepts.authority_holder: Operator's accountable OT or compliance executive authorizes production use and control changes.
concepts.distributor: SCADA integrators, energy consultancies and regional renewable-installation networks
concepts.risk_bearer: The operator bears operational and regulatory consequences; the AI supplier bears contracted product obligations.
concepts.transaction_owner: Operator program manager accountable for moving the pilot into production
concepts.first_paid_event: A steering committee sets a production-readiness gate for an AI pilot.
concepts.acquisition_route: Sell a bounded pilot through OT integrators that already own deployment milestones
concepts.compounding_asset: A sector-specific library connecting control patterns, data-quality exceptions, overrides and audit outcomes
hypotheses: Smaller operators lack a usable system of record for deployer controls.
An OT integrator will resell the ledger rather than build it.
Production-readiness budgets exist independently of general legal advice.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: applicable critical-infrastructure AI duties; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: reliable integration with OT logs; REPUTATIONAL EXPECTATION: operator accountability; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: infrequent pilots may lengthen sales cycles.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not claim the ledger certifies operational safety or replace the operator's engineering and legal judgment.

concepts.title: Machine-AI Release Passport
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A release passport for smaller industrial-equipment makers records model changes, intended purpose, validation and responsible sign-offs so an AI-enabled machine update can clear design release without reconstructing its history.
concepts.customer: European SME manufacturers of industrial machines containing AI-enabled inspection, control or robotics functions
concepts.loss_event: A product release or customer acceptance is delayed because AI changes cannot be traced to classification, validation and accountable approval evidence.
concepts.payer: Head of engineering, quality or regulatory affairs
concepts.beneficiary: Manufacturer, distributor, industrial buyer and machine users
concepts.authority_holder: Manufacturer's designated product-release or quality authority
concepts.distributor: Machinery conformity advisers, automation integrators and notified-body preparation consultants
concepts.risk_bearer: The manufacturer bears release, recall and conformity exposure; the industrial buyer bears downtime risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: Product manager who owns the release milestone
concepts.first_paid_event: Design freeze, major model update or a buyer's factory-acceptance review exposes missing evidence.
concepts.acquisition_route: Embed a paid passport sprint into machinery conformity and automation-consulting engagements
concepts.compounding_asset: A structured dataset of model-change types, evidence requirements, reviewer objections and accepted release patterns
hypotheses: Machine builders will prepare materially before the 2028 application date.
Existing product-lifecycle tools leave an AI-specific evidence gap.
Conformity advisers can provide low-cost distribution.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: final rules applicable to covered product AI; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: evidence capture across engineering tools; SOFT INDUSTRY NORM: design-freeze review; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: long machinery release cycles.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not treat the Commission's examples as exhaustive or market the passport as a conformity assessment.

concepts.title: Biometric AI Role-and-Warranty Map
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A transaction-specific contract map helps biometric access vendors and building operators allocate AI provider, deployer, evidence, change-notice and indemnity duties before a deployment contract is signed.
concepts.customer: Biometric workplace and building-access vendors selling into the EU
concepts.loss_event: A deployment deal stalls or leaves uninsured liability because the parties disagree about AI roles, intended use, data flows and control ownership.
concepts.payer: Vendor general counsel, product counsel or enterprise deal lead
concepts.beneficiary: Vendor, building operator, workforce and visitors
concepts.authority_holder: Each party's authorized legal signatory controls acceptance of the role and warranty allocation.
concepts.distributor: Privacy counsel, security-system integrators and commercial insurance brokers
concepts.risk_bearer: Vendor and operator bear allocated contractual and regulatory exposure; affected people bear rights and access harms.
concepts.transaction_owner: Commercial lead accountable for closing the deployment agreement
concepts.first_paid_event: A buyer returns contract redlines disputing AI responsibility, audit access or model-change notice.
concepts.acquisition_route: White-label the map to privacy boutiques and security integrators on live contract redlines
concepts.compounding_asset: A clause-and-outcome graph linking deployment facts to negotiated roles, warranties and recurring objections
hypotheses: Role ambiguity is a recurring close blocker rather than a one-off legal question.
Counsel will license structured precedent support.
Redacted negotiation outcomes can improve future mappings.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: applicable biometric AI and data-protection duties; ASSUMED CONVENTION: negotiated warranty allocation; REPUTATIONAL EXPECTATION: rights-sensitive use; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: legal-service substitution risk.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not facilitate prohibited biometric uses or present contractual allocation as eliminating non-transferable statutory duties.

concepts.title: Solar Inverter CRA Incident Relay
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A telemetry-to-reporting relay for solar-inverter manufacturers assembles a clocked incident record, responsible-person decision and CRA submission packet when field installers surface a severe incident or exploited vulnerability.
concepts.customer: Small European manufacturers and own-brand importers of connected solar inverters and energy controllers
concepts.loss_event: A security signal remains in installer email or support tickets until the 24-hour or 72-hour reporting window is missed.
concepts.payer: Manufacturer security lead, product director or managing director
concepts.beneficiary: Manufacturer, installers, system owners and electricity users
concepts.authority_holder: Manufacturer's designated security incident authority decides reportability and approves submission.
concepts.distributor: Renewable installers, inverter service networks and product-security consultancies
concepts.risk_bearer: The manufacturer bears reporting exposure; system owners and installers bear operational disruption.
concepts.transaction_owner: Head of product security who owns incident closure
concepts.first_paid_event: Annual readiness contract signed before coverage begins, with a paid activation fee on a qualifying alert.
concepts.acquisition_route: Pilot through a regional installation firm and sell upstream via inverter distributors and service partners
concepts.compounding_asset: A labeled corpus of field signals, severity decisions, evidence requests, corrective actions and reporting timelines
concepts.mechanism_class: Sector-specific incident decision and reporting relay
hypotheses: Installer-originated signals are a material blind spot for smaller manufacturers.
Manufacturers will pay a readiness retainer before an incident.
The incident corpus can improve triage without exposing customer secrets.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: CRA reporting deadlines for covered manufacturers; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: trustworthy signal ingestion and clock start; ASSUMED CONVENTION: installer participation; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: low incident frequency challenges usage pricing.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not autonomously decide legal reportability or transmit sensitive incident data without the manufacturer's authorized approval.

concepts.title: Smart-Building Vulnerability Intake Network
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A branded intake and escalation network gives controller and sensor manufacturers one monitored channel through which installers, integrators and researchers can submit vulnerability evidence that reaches the accountable incident owner.
concepts.customer: SME manufacturers of connected HVAC, access, lighting and building-control products
concepts.loss_event: A credible vulnerability report is lost, duplicated or mishandled across support channels, delaying triage and any required CRA notification.
concepts.payer: Product security manager or chief technology officer
concepts.beneficiary: Manufacturer, integrators, building operators and occupants
concepts.authority_holder: Manufacturer's product-security authority determines severity, exploitation status and escalation.
concepts.risk_bearer: The manufacturer bears product and reporting exposure; building operators bear service and safety disruption.
concepts.transaction_owner: Security operations owner accountable for vulnerability-case closure
concepts.first_paid_event: The manufacturer launches a monitored disclosure channel or fails an enterprise buyer's supplier-security review.
concepts.acquisition_route: Bundle the service with integrator supplier reviews and product-security readiness assessments
concepts.compounding_asset: A device-category taxonomy linking intake quality, duplicate patterns, triage outcomes and remediation latency
hypotheses: Fragmented external intake is a larger bottleneck than SRP form completion.
Integrators can require or recommend the channel to suppliers.
Manufacturers accept a shared network with strict data separation.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: applicable CRA manufacturer reporting; SOFT INDUSTRY NORM: coordinated disclosure practice; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: secure intake and deduplication; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: crowded disclosure-tool market.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not encourage unauthorized testing or disclose vulnerability details beyond consented, need-to-know reporting channels.

concepts.title: B2B Software CRA Clockroom
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A managed clockroom for small B2B software publishers converts security alerts into an auditable awareness timestamp, 24-hour decision queue, 72-hour evidence packet and final-report follow-up.
concepts.customer: European B2B software publishers whose products fall within the CRA
concepts.loss_event: Ambiguous internal awareness and scattered technical evidence cause a missed notification deadline or an unsupported report.
concepts.payer: Chief technology officer, security lead or founder
concepts.beneficiary: Publisher, enterprise customers and downstream users
concepts.authority_holder: Publisher's appointed incident commander approves reportability decisions and submissions.
concepts.distributor: Managed security providers, penetration-testing firms and cyber-insurance brokers
concepts.risk_bearer: The publisher bears statutory and contractual exposure; customers bear exploitation and downtime loss.
concepts.transaction_owner: Incident commander who owns the case from awareness through final report
concepts.first_paid_event: A yearly readiness subscription starts after a tabletop exercise exposes timing or evidence gaps.
concepts.acquisition_route: Offer a co-branded tabletop-to-subscription conversion through managed security providers
concepts.compounding_asset: A rules-and-workflow engine trained on redacted incident timelines, missing evidence and authority decisions
hypotheses: Small publishers cannot staff continuous CRA deadline coordination.
Managed security providers prefer a partner workflow to building one.
Tabletop failures predict subscription conversion.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: covered-manufacturer deadlines; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: defensible awareness timestamps; ASSUMED CONVENTION: outsourced coordination is acceptable; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: small-publisher budgets.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not promise that workflow timestamps bind authorities or replace incident containment and professional legal assessment.

concepts.title: Industrial Gateway Emergency Evidence Retainer
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: An on-call evidence retainer gives makers of remote-maintenance gateways a pre-assigned incident cell that can reconstruct affected versions, EU distribution and corrective-action facts inside the CRA reporting windows.
concepts.customer: SME manufacturers of industrial remote-access, machine-monitoring and maintenance gateways
concepts.loss_event: A severe gateway incident triggers customer escalation while the manufacturer cannot quickly identify affected versions, markets or corrective-action ownership.
concepts.payer: Chief operating officer or product-security leader
concepts.beneficiary: Manufacturer, machine builders, factories and maintenance teams
concepts.authority_holder: Manufacturer incident executive approves scope, reporting decisions and corrective-action statements.
concepts.distributor: Industrial cybersecurity assessors, machinery insurers and automation distributors
concepts.risk_bearer: The gateway manufacturer bears product and reporting exposure; factories bear downtime and compromise risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: Operations executive accountable for customer and authority incident response
concepts.first_paid_event: A distributor, insurer or enterprise customer requires demonstrated emergency reporting readiness.
concepts.acquisition_route: Sell through industrial cyber assessors after a tabletop drill or supplier-security finding
concepts.compounding_asset: A reusable dependency, version, distribution and corrective-action evidence graph for industrial gateways
hypotheses: Version and EU-market reconstruction is a repeatable incident bottleneck.
Contractual readiness requirements can trigger payment before an incident.
A small expert cell can serve multiple manufacturers without conflicts.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: CRA reporting for covered manufacturers; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: accurate product and distribution inventory; REPUTATIONAL EXPECTATION: rapid customer communication; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: retainers compete with general incident-response firms.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not access customer systems without explicit authorization or conflate regulatory reporting with complete forensic investigation.

concepts.title: Private-Label IoT Incident Chain Registry
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A supplier-chain registry helps EU private-label IoT brands pre-map who detects, escalates, evidences and authorizes a CRA incident report across overseas factories, firmware vendors and the brand owner.
concepts.customer: EU private-label brands selling connected home, fitness or consumer-electronics products
concepts.loss_event: An exploited vulnerability crosses supplier boundaries with no enforceable evidence route, leaving the accountable manufacturer unable to meet reporting windows.
concepts.payer: Brand compliance director, sourcing director or general counsel
concepts.authority_holder: The legally accountable manufacturer's designated incident authority approves reporting; supplier duties remain contractual.
concepts.distributor: Product-compliance labs, sourcing agents and retailer supplier-assurance teams
concepts.risk_bearer: The accountable manufacturer bears statutory exposure; suppliers bear negotiated contractual exposure; consumers bear security harm.
concepts.transaction_owner: Sourcing or compliance director who owns supplier onboarding and incident clauses
concepts.first_paid_event: A new supplier or product line is approved only after the incident chain and evidence duties are mapped.
concepts.acquisition_route: Embed the registry in compliance-lab onboarding and retailer supplier-assurance programs
concepts.compounding_asset: A cross-supplier graph of product components, responsible entities, response times, clause failures and evidence handoffs
hypotheses: Private-label brands cannot reliably reconstruct incident ownership from current contracts.
Retailers or labs will make the registry an onboarding requirement.
Suppliers will maintain the mapping when tied to purchase-order eligibility.
concepts.constraint_class: LAW / BINDING RULE: CRA duties of the legally accountable covered entity; ASSUMED CONVENTION: private-label role allocation requires case verification; TECHNICAL LIMITATION: supplier data freshness; ECONOMIC LIMITATION: onboarding friction may deter adoption.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not assume an importer, distributor or brand is the statutory manufacturer without product-specific legal verification, and must not shift non-transferable duties by contract.
